CTFs & lab notes

Embedded Security Home Lab

Planned documentation of a small embedded security lab, combining development boards, external flash, serial access, logic analysis, and basic SDR equipment.

To be continued…

Planned scope

The planned setup includes an ARM or ESP32 development board, external SPI Flash, a USB-to-TTL adapter, a logic analyzer, and a basic SDR. Future notes will document connections, test conditions, and repeatable experiments.

Draft outline

This is a structured draft. Each section will be completed with measured results, commands, and evidence as the work is carried out.

Bench layout

  • Define the bench area, power distribution, and grounding.
  • List instruments and their calibration status.
  • Record cable and adapter inventory.

Target boards

  • Select ARM and ESP32 development boards.
  • Document boot modes, debug interfaces, and firmware tooling.
  • Prepare a known-good reference image.

External flash and serial access

  • Wire SPI flash for read-only access.
  • Set up USB-to-TTL console capture.
  • Record pinouts and voltage levels.

Logic analysis and SDR

  • Attach a logic analyzer to the target buses.
  • Configure a basic SDR receive chain.
  • Document sample rates, triggers, and limits.

Repeatable experiments

  • Write a setup checklist and teardown procedure.
  • Store captures with hashes and notes.
  • Record safety limits and known failure modes.

Topics to cover

  • ARM and ESP32 development boards
  • External SPI Flash
  • USB-to-TTL and UART
  • Logic analyzer
  • Basic SDR
